rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice to terminate. Just cause is either at-fault cause (such as default in rent, breach of a material lease term, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, or refusal to renew a similar lease) or no-fault cause (owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court order, or intent to demolish or substantially remodel).
rules.key_value: 12 months of continuous and lawful occupancy (or, if adult tenants are added before 24 months, all tenants 12 months or more, or one or more tenants 24 months or more)
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property where the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied it for 12 months; if additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant has occupied for 24 months, applies only if all tenants have occupied 12 months or more or one or more tenants have occupied 24 months or more.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, or adult residential facilities; dormitories owned and operated by higher education institutions or K-12 schools; housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with an owner who lives there; single-family owner-occupied residences (including where the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms, and mobilehomes); owner-occupied two-unit properties in a single structure (neither unit an ADU or JADU); housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless a mobilehome; separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, where tenants received the required written exemption notice; deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable housing or housing subject to an affordable housing subsidy agreement.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply renders the written termination notice void. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees and costs in the court's discretion, and up to three times actual damages plus punitive damages for willful conduct or oppression, fraud, or malice; the Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.title: Notice and opportunity to cure for curable lease violations
rules.requirement: Before issuing a notice to terminate for a curable lease violation, the owner must first give notice of the violation with an opportunity to cure; if not cured within the time set in the notice, a three-day notice to quit without an opportunity to cure may then be served.
rules.key_value: three-day notice to quit after uncured violation
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to the just cause requirement terminating for a curable lease violation.

rules.penalty: An owner's failure to comply with any provision of this section shall render the written termination notice void.
rules.quoted_span: If the violation is not cured within the time period set forth in the notice, a three-day notice to quit without an opportunity to cure may thereafter be served to terminate the tenancy.

rules.title: Relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault just cause termination
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the owner must, regardless of tenant income, either make a direct relocation payment or waive in writing the final month's rent, equal to one month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued; any relocation assistance must be provided within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, and the notice must inform the tenant of this right.
rules.key_value: one month of the tenant's rent
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies for which just cause is required under subdivision (a) where the owner issues a termination notice based on no-fault just cause.

rules.penalty: An owner's failure to strictly comply with this subdivision shall render the notice of termination void.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: The relocation assistance or rent waiver required by this subdivision shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.

rules.title: Required tenant notice of just cause and rent cap protections
rules.requirement: Owners of residential real property subject to this section must notify tenants, in the lease, an addendum, or a signed written notice, in no less than 12-point type, using the prescribed statement about California rent increase limits and just cause requirements; for tenancies existing prior to July 1, 2020, written notice was due no later than August 1, 2020.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to section 1946.2, for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020 (July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes) and tenancies existing before those dates.
